To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cell adhesion molecule CD44 is overexpressed in the majority of prostate cancers, and is associated with poor clinical outcome, that CD44 is an important mediator of prostate cancer metastasis, that CD44 can be targeted by antibodies, and that antibodies against CD44 are effective in inhibiting prostate cancer cell adhesion and metastasis.
prostate cancer cells express cell adhesion molecules that promote cancer metastasis, and that prostate cancer cells have adhesion abnormalities that promote their metastasis.
the adhesion molecules E-cadherin and beta1-integrin play a role in the development and metastasis of prostate cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular and cellular basis of cancer metastasis.
understanding the molecular and cellular function and the biological significance of cell adhesion in normal and malignant prostate tissue.
the molecular and cellular function, regulation, and role in prostate cancer of cell adhesion molecule and adhesion abnormalities.

prostate cancer cells express cell adhesion molecules that mediate cell-cell and cell-matrix adhesions, which are involved in the regulation of cell growth, differentiation and migration.
cell adhesion molecules are involved in cancer metastasis and that their role is multifactorial.
prostate cancer is a heterogeneous disease with a complex molecular basis.

prostate cancer cells express a number of adhesion molecules that are differentially expressed in normal epithelial cells.
prostate cancer is a heterogeneous disease with multiple pathways of metastasis and invasion, and that the role of cell-cell adhesion molecules in prostate cancer is not fully understood.

the expression of cell adhesion molecule in prostate cancer may be a useful prognostic factor and that the development of novel therapeutic strategies targeting cell adhesion molecule may improve the outcome of patients with prostate cancer.
